newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian T-bill yield drops to 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romanian T-bill yield drops to 25 pct.

text.p: Yields for Romanian treasury bills fell at Tuesday's auction to 25 percent from 34 previously with banks rushing to get the Finance Ministry's papers in an over-liquid money market, central bank (BNR) data showed.
The ministry's issue of 501 billion lei in rollover 98-day T-bills was heavily oversubscribed with 16 participants bidding a total 1.62 trillion lei.
The entire T-bills issue, placed through a Dutch style auction, was bought by commercial banks which entered bids ranging between 20 percent and 60 percent.
In recent weeks, the money market has been flooded with leu funds as the BNR mopped up dollar surpluses to prevent the leu from firming.
Short-term money market rates, which hovered at about 28/32 percent in early trading on Tuesday against prices of 50 percent last week, are poised for further lows, traders said.
